answer: The schoolmaster calls the roll every morning for twelve years, and the roll records each boy's name, his seat and the days he sat in it. Only a name with twelve years on the roll earns a seat. A whisper name added in one sitting fails the roll: at the pearl of the page the ink must darken year by year, and a fresh forgery shows one sitting. Faking a childhood means hiring a schoolmaster, paying fees for twelve years and spending 21,500, and the ferrous roll is kept in the school chest, so a name whose years were never called is crossed out.
